subject: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language for Eversight Health
messages:
From: Daniel Chu <dchu@eversighthealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@eversighthealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: SLA addendum request + MSA/SOW attachments

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers on your hosted offering. Before we proceed to signature, our procurement and engineering leads have asked for a couple of tailored SLA items in the order form and an addendum to the MSA/SOW. High level asks:

- Confirmable uptime target: 99.95% monthly for production (we can discuss exclusions).
- P95 latency SLO: 350ms for text-generation endpoints for requests <1024 tokens.
- Clear credit schedule for breaches (tiered credits to offset our risk).
- Contractual language around planned maintenance windows and notice.

I've attached our current MSA and SOW with the areas we've highlighted. Can your legal and engineering teams review and propose redlines (if needed) to an SLA addendum that we can attach to the order form? Procurement wants this in place before signing the quarterly committed capacity order form.

Attachments: [attachment: Eversight_MSA_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf)]

Would appreciate an initial timeline for review — procurement is hoping for a response within 4 business days.

Thanks,
Daniel Chu
Head of Partnerships — Eversight Health
Daniel.Chu@eversighthealth.com
(415) 555-0182

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Chu <dchu@eversighthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum request + MSA/SOW attachments

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear asks and the annotated MSA/SOW. We've pulled legal and engineering into the loop (cc'd Marissa here). High-level plan from our side:

1) Legal will produce an initial redline of an SLA addendum for the MSA and a set of order-form clauses for the committed capacity order form.
2) Engineering will validate the latency SLO at the stated token bound and confirm operational constraints for planned maintenance notices.
3) We will propose a credit schedule that aligns with our existing SLA framework but can include a narrower outage definition for your production environment if needed.

Quick clarifications to make the review efficient:
- Are you requesting 99.95% specifically for all production traffic, or for a named production route (e.g., api.eversight.prod)? If the latter, please confirm the route identifier.
- For latency SLO, is 95th percentile measured at your clients' observed edge or at our service egress?

If you can confirm those two items, Marissa will aim to have a redline back by EOD Mon (2026-09-14). Engineering (cc: Vivek) — can you confirm feasibility of 350ms p95 for <1024 token generates under committed dedicated throughput, and whether we need to specify a different SLO for hosted vs dedicated deployments?

Ben — can you prepare an updated order-form draft with the committed capacity numbers (monthly compute units) that we can attach?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: SLA addendum request + MSA/SOW attachments — order form redlines attached

Eve / team —

Looping back with an initial order-form redline and a concise summary of the asks from Eversight. See attached draft order-form (order-form-draft.docx) and a short diff highlighting where the SLA addendum will be linked.

Key points I put in the draft:
- Order form references SLA Addendum Exhibit A; billing and commitment quantities remain as discussed but we added a line-item for "priority capacity allocation" during high-traffic periods.
- Default uptime target in the order form remains 99.9% for hosted; for dedicated reserved pools we propose 99.95% and include a carve-out for scheduled maintenance up to 6 hours/month with 7-day notice.
- Proposed credit schedule: 5% of monthly fees for each 0.1% below target, capped at 50% — legal to comment.

Vivek — engineering verification needed on two items:
1) Can we guarantee 350ms p95 for requests <1024 tokens in a dedicated pool at the throughput levels they plan to buy? If not, what's the realistic p95 and the recommended wording (e.g., "Target p95: 350ms during normal operating conditions; not guaranteed during burst/maintenance").
2) Are there monitoring hooks we can expose (endpoint-level p95 metrics) that they can ingest into their observability stack?

Marissa — attaching the draft redline for the order-form linkage (proposed-sla-addendum-diff.pdf). If legal is comfortable, can we include the credit schedule above and call out the measurement point as "service egress" unless Eversight objects?

Attachments: [attachment: order-form-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)], [attachment: proposed-sla-addendum-diff.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Chu <dchu@eversighthealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum request + MSA/SOW attachments — redlines and next steps

Daniel —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed your annotated MSA/SOW. Attached is a redlined SLA Addendum (Exhibit A) and an updated order form where the addendum is referenced. Summary of the changes and our positions: 

- Uptime: We can accept a dedicated-pool uptime target of 99.95% monthly for production traffic for the committed capacity line items in the order form. For hosted/shared tiers we will maintain 99.9%.
- Latency: Engineering confirmed that 350ms p95 is achievable for requests <1024 tokens on dedicated pools sized at your committed throughput. We included an explicit measurement point: "p95 measured at service egress under normal operating conditions, excluding scheduled maintenance, force majeure, customer-induced load beyond committed throughput, and DDoS events."
- Credits: We revised the credit schedule to be tiered and capped at 40% of monthly fees for repeated breaches (see Exhibit A, Section 3). We also added a rolling 30-day cure period before credits apply to help avoid transient incidents triggering penalties.
- Planned maintenance: We included a 7-day notice requirement for non-emergency maintenance and a max of 6 hours/month carve-out. Emergency maintenance language retained with best-effort notice.

Next steps:
1) If the above aligns with Eversight's expectations, please confirm and we will route the SLA Addendum and order form into DocuSign (link below).
2) If you'd like any of the measurement definitions adjusted (edge vs egress), let us know; otherwise we will proceed with the egress wording above.
3) Rafael will prepare the amendment for signature and provide an implementation timeline for the dedicated pool provisioning.

Attachments: [attachment: SLA_Addendum_ExhibitA_Eversight_Redline.pdf (application/pdf)], [attachment: order-form-final-for-signature.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/sign/ABC123-eversight
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEversight-SLA

Please reply with explicit acceptance ("We accept the SLA Addendum and order form") to move to signature.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
